claude_fable_5.1_high/001:
My policy is built around the well-known structure of Dots and Boxes (chains, loops, control, double-dealing) and a fast bitmask alpha-beta search:

1. **State encoding** – the 40 edges are packed into a single integer bitmask; box side-counts are updated incrementally. A transposition table (keyed by the edge mask, whose value is "net future boxes for the player to move") collapses move-order permutations.
2. **Move generation with theory-based pruning**
   * If a box can be captured: candidates are the captures plus the *double-dealing* moves (leave the last 2 boxes of a chain / 4 of a loop) – the only alternatives that can ever be better.
   * If no captures but safe moves exist (the "fight for control" phase): safe moves plus sacrifices of fully formed chains/loops (hard-hearted and half-hearted handouts for 2-chains).
   * If no safe moves (endgame): components are decomposed into chains/loops and only canonical opening edges are searched, so the endgame is solved **exactly**.
3. **Search** – iterative-deepening negamax with alpha-beta and TT; depth is only consumed by "fight" moves, capture sequences and endgame openings are searched to the end. Leaves still in the fight phase are evaluated with the **long-chain parity rule** (who will receive the first long chain, computed from remaining edges/boxes and detected long chains/loops) weighted by the value of control and a confidence factor. The search stops early when the result is provably exact, and uses partial results with a 0.7 s deadline.
4. **Safety** – convention detection for the 5x5 array indexing (with a hedge preferring moves valid under both conventions until detected), final legality validation and multi-level fallbacks so a legal move is always returned.
claude_fable_5.1_high/002:
The policy treats the position as a bitmask of the 40 edges and runs a negamax alpha‑beta search (iterative deepening, transposition table, ~0.6 s budget). The value of a position is "net boxes the player to move will gain from here", so the transposition table can be keyed on the edge mask alone.

Key ideas:
1. **Move reduction with proper endgame theory.** When boxes are capturable, the only moves considered are captures and *hard‑hearted handouts* (non‑capturing moves that leave all 3‑sided boxes as double‑cross pairs). This is exactly what lets the engine keep control at the end of chains/loops (take all‑but‑2 / all‑but‑4) and lets it deny double‑crosses by opening 2‑chains in the middle. Any other non‑capturing move is dominated, so the search stays small.
2. **Depth counts only non‑capturing moves**, so capture sequences are followed to the end (quiescence). In the late game the search solves the position exactly (detected automatically, and then stops early).
3. **Heuristic at cutoff** (opening/midgame): estimates who will get control from the parity of remaining safe edges and scores it with the long‑chain/loop structure (controller keeps everything except 2 per long chain / 4 per loop). Ties at the root are broken by preferring moves that keep the most safe edges (avoids committing to 2‑sided boxes early).
4. **Safety:** convention auto‑check against the capture array, and a fallback that always returns a legal empty edge.
claude_fable_5.1_high/003:
My policy models the position as a 40-bit edge mask plus per-box side counts and runs a negamax alpha-beta search (with a transposition table keyed on the edge set, since the future value for the player to move depends only on which edges are drawn):

1. **Forced-capture handling**: when a box can be captured, the search considers a single canonical capture (preferring "ending"/double captures so chains are consumed correctly) plus *decline* moves — non-capturing moves after which every 3-sided box is paired across its open edge (this exactly generates the "all-but-2" chain double-cross and "all-but-4" loop declines). Everything else is pruned.
2. **Exact endgame**: once no safe moves remain (every edge would create a 3-sided box), the search is exact (unlimited depth), so chain/loop sacrificing order and control-keeping double-crosses are played perfectly.
3. **Safe phase**: depth-limited iterative deepening over safe moves (plus small sacrifices of ≤2-box components when few safe moves are left). The leaf evaluation implements the long-chain/parity rule: using `turns = edges_left − boxes_left + double-crosses`, I predict who ends up in control given the currently formed long chains and loops, and estimate the resulting box swing.
4. Time-controlled iterative deepening (with a fallback greedy move), plus convention detection for the array padding so moves are always legal.
claude_fable_5.1_high/004:
My policy treats the 4x4 board as a 40‑edge bitmask and runs an iterative‑deepening alpha‑beta (negamax) search with a transposition table under a strict time budget (~0.5 s), always falling back to a safe heuristic move so a legal move is guaranteed.

Key ideas built into the search:
1. **Capture handling with control**: when a box can be completed, the only moves considered are (a) capturing moves and (b) "double‑dealing" declines (moves that deliberately leave a double‑cross edge, i.e. give up the last 2 boxes of a chain / 4 of a loop) – the classic way to keep control at the end of the game. Capturing moves don't consume search depth, so chains are resolved fully.
2. **Safe vs. unsafe moves**: when no capture exists, moves are ordered safe (don't create a 3‑sided box) before unsafe (sacrifices), and the search decides whether a sacrifice is worthwhile.
3. **Evaluation**: at leaves, if safe moves remain, a parity term estimates who will be forced to open the first chain (the player who makes the last safe move gains control); if no safe move exists, the evaluation is minus the smallest component that must be handed over (via greedy chain-following simulation).
4. **Endgame exactness**: once few edges remain, the search solves the loony endgame exactly (which chain to open, hard‑hearted vs. half‑hearted handouts, when to take all vs. keep control), storing exact values in the transposition table.
5. **Robustness**: every returned move is verified to be an empty edge; multiple fallbacks ensure legality.
claude_fable_5.1_high/005:
My policy treats the position as a bitmask of the 40 edges and plays with a combination of exact Dots-and-Boxes theory and search:

1. **Capture handling (theory-based, instant):** Any 3-sided box is taken immediately *unless* it is one of the last two boxes of a chain (or last four of a loop), where the classic *double-deal* (leave 2 / leave 4 to keep control) is a real option. Only those decision points are branched on in the search; everything else is forced.
2. **Move canonicalization:** Non-capturing moves are split into *safe* moves (no box gets a 3rd side) and *sacrifices*. Sacrifices are grouped into components (chains/loops of 2-sided boxes) and only one representative edge per component is searched (the hard-hearted handout for 2-chains), since all openings of a component lead to identical resulting positions.
3. **Search:** Negamax alpha-beta with a transposition table and iterative deepening on turn depth, under a time budget (~0.7 s). Once a position is "loony" (no safe moves left) the search runs to the end of the game exactly, so the whole endgame (chain/loop control fight, double-crosses) is solved perfectly. With few edges left the entire game is solved exactly.
4. **Mid-game heuristic:** At depth-limited leaves the evaluation estimates who will be forced to open the first chain via the parity of remaining safe moves and weights it by how much control is worth (remaining boxes minus long-chain concessions). Move ordering prefers edges touching low-sided boxes to avoid forming chains prematurely.
5. **Safety:** Every returned move is validated against the input arrays, with fallbacks to guarantee a legal move string.
